Subject: Exhibitor Application Inquiry, GEGYjiji / Watercolor Illustration

Dear Tokyo Art Book Fair team,

Tokyo Art Book Fair's reputation for bringing together independent artists and publishers in a serious, discovery-oriented context makes it exactly the kind of platform I have been working toward. I am a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and since 2020 I have maintained a daily painting practice, a series called "diary", that grew into my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, published in October 2021; the seriality and everyday observation at the heart of that work feels well-suited to the artist book format your fair values. My paintings move through ordinary scenes, ordinary, everyday scenes, the particular quality of light in a familiar street, and try to make those places feel like somewhere the viewer half-remembers. A selection of my work is visible on Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/gegyjiji/. I would be grateful to know whether exhibitor applications for 2026 are currently open, where I can find the submission details, and whether there is a deadline I should be aware of.

Thank you for your time.

GEGYjiji

midterm_wave.email_en:
Subject: Inquiry from illustrator GEGYjiji, watercolor zine / consignment possibility

Dear UTRECHT team,

I have long admired how UTRECHT brings together artist books, zines, and illustrated works that sit quietly between fine art and everyday life, and I think my work may belong in that same conversation. I am GEGYjiji, a Chinese watercolor artist based in Tokyo, and in 2021 I published Colour Diary, a small illustration collection grown from a daily watercolor practice that documents domestic interiors, neighborhood light, and the quiet texture of city life, much of it observed here in Tokyo. My work has been shown in Tokyo most recently as part of Tide from China, a group exhibition at ACG_Labo in Harajuku in 2023, and I am now looking to place printed work or original pieces in spaces where that kind of attentive, intimate scale feels at home. I would love to explore whether a consignment arrangement or a small exhibition might be a possibility, and you are welcome to see more of my work on Instagram at @gegyjiji. Thank you very much for your time, and I hope to hear from you.

GEGYjiji
midterm_wave.email_ja:
件名: 水彩イラスト集『Colour Diary』のお取り扱いについてのご相談

UTRECHTご担当者様

UTRECHTさんが扱われるアーティストブックやZINEの選書を拝見し、日常のなかに宿る美しさを丁寧にすくいとった作品たちが並ぶ空間に、自分の本を置いていただけないかと思いご連絡いたしました。私はGEGYjiji（ジェジー）と申します。中国・湖南省出身、現在は東京を拠点に活動している水彩イラストレーターです。2020年から毎日水彩画を描き続けており、ありふれた日常の風景といったごく普通の日常の景色を、心に残る一枚へと変えていくこの「diary」という実践から、2021年10月に初のイラスト集『Colour Diary』が生まれました。作品はInstagram（@gegyjiji）でもご覧いただけます。UTRECHTさんの棚に並ぶ本の一冊として、この小さな日々の記録をお届けできればと思い、お取り扱いやご相談の機会をいただけますと大変嬉しく存じます。

どうぞよろしくお願いいたします。

GEGYjiji

Hello TOKIO ART BOOK FAIR team,

I came across your fair and was drawn to its invitation-based format and the kind of intimate, artist-made publications it brings together, it feels like exactly the right context for the work I make. You can find my recent work on Instagram at @gegyjiji, and I am happy to share any additional materials you might need.

Thank you for your time, and I hope to hear from you.

GEGYjiji

Subject: Exhibitor Inquiry, Little Tokyo Zine Fest 2026

Dear Little Tokyo Zine Fest team,

Little Tokyo Zine Fest's focus on small-edition print work and intimate artist tables feels like the right context for what I make: daily watercolor paintings that move through ordinary scenes, red walls, alleyways, pools, the particular light of a familiar street corner, and try to make something emotionally true from them. Since 2020 I have kept a daily watercolor practice called "diary," and my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary (October 2021), grew directly from that habit of looking slowly at everyday life. I would like to apply for a Full-Table vendor spot at the 2026 event and would be grateful to know the application process, table fee, and whether a finished publication is required to apply. Recent work is on Instagram at https://www.instagram.com/gegyjiji/ if it helps to see the practice before we correspond further. Please let me know what the next step looks like, I am happy to send any additional materials you need.

GEGYjiji

exploration_layer.email_en:
Subject: Consignment Inquiry, Colour Diary / GEGYjiji

Dear B&B team,

I have long admired how your shelves bring together books, zines, and art in a way that feels genuinely curated rather than simply stocked, and Shimokitazawa feels like the right neighborhood for the kind of quiet, observational work I make. I am GEGYjiji, a Tokyo-based Chinese watercolor artist, and I am writing to ask whether B&B accepts consignment inquiries for self-published artist books. My first illustration collection, Colour Diary, grew out of a daily watercolor diary practice I began in 2020, it documents domestic interiors, neighborhood light, and small moments of urban life in a format I think would sit naturally alongside the books you carry. You can find a fuller sense of my work on Instagram at @gegyjiji. I would love to hear about your current process for consignment, and I am also happy to visit the shop in person if that would be easier.

Warm regards,
GEGYjiji

exploration_layer.email_en:
Subject: Inquiry Regarding Exhibition or Residency Opportunity, GEGYjiji (Watercolor Artist, Tokyo)

Dear Koganecho Area Management Center,

I write with admiration for the work you have sustained in Kogane-cho, the way your programming treats the neighborhood itself as living subject, drawing artists into genuine conversation with its streets and residents, is an approach I find deeply aligned with my own practice. Since 2020 I have maintained a daily watercolor series called "diary," painting the ordinary scenes that surround me, ordinary, everyday scenes, the particular quality of light in a familiar street corner, with the aim of making the utterly unremarkable feel moving and worth dwelling in. This practice grew into my first solo illustration collection, Colour Diary, published in October 2021, and I believe the same attentiveness that drives that work would respond well to Kogane-cho's layered urban landscape. I am writing to inquire whether you have current or forthcoming opportunities, exhibition, residency, or site-responsive project, for which my work might be considered, and I would be glad to share further materials at your request. My watercolor practice can be followed at Instagram @gegyjiji (https://www.instagram.com/gegyjiji/).

With respect and gratitude for your time,
GEGYjiji
